docs.title: cvl
docs.text: An extremely small Computer Vision Library, written in C.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Image representation — A unified type for grayscale and color image data.
  • Image I/O — Read and write supported image formats.
  • Image Processing — Color conversion, thresholding, filtering, morphological operations.
  • Analysis — Connected component labeling, Sobel gradient magnitude.
  • Command-line interface — A comanion cvl executable for working with images.

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text: The following examples demonstrate how CVL operations can be combined into practical image-procesing workflows.

docs.title: Edge Detection
docs.text: Edge detection identifies locations of significant intensity changes in an image.

docs.title: Sobel Operator
docs.text:
The Sobel operator estimates image gradients using horizontal and vertical convolution kernels. These gradients can be combined to estimate edge magnitude and direction.

Original Smoothed grayscale Magnitudes 
#include <cvl/cvl.h>

int main(void) {
    // Load Input Image.
    cvl_Mat img = cvl_imread("./data/original/halo.ppm");
    cvl_Mat gray = cvl_cvt_color_new(&img, CVL_COLOR_RGB2GRAY);
    cvl_Mat blur = cvl_blur_gauss_new(&gray, 0.0, 1.0);

    // Apply Sobel Filter (for gradient magnitudes).
    cvl_Mat sobel = cvl_sobel_mag_new(&blur);

    // Save Results.
    cvl_imwrite("./data/modified/1-original.ppm", &img);
    cvl_imwrite("./data/modified/2-blur.pgm", &blur);
    cvl_imwrite("./data/modified/5-mags.pgm", &sobel);

    // Cleanup.
    cvl_mat_free(&sobel);
    cvl_mat_free(&blur);
    cvl_mat_free(&gray);
    cvl_mat_free(&img);

    return 0;
}

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers building CVL, running its tests and examples, and using the library in a small C program.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
CVL can be built from source using CMake:

git clone https://github.com/OwenMastropietro/cvl.git
cd cvl

cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build

This builds the static library and the cvl command-line tool.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
To build and run tests:

cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

Note: GoogleTest is fetched during CMake configuration, so building the tests requires network access.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
CVL includes example programs demonstrating common image-processing operations.

To build the example programs:

cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build

Example executables are built in build/examples/.

Run an example:

./build/examples/cvl_blur

See Examples for an overview of the available demonstrations.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
To install CVL:

cmake --install build --prefix /usr/local

This installs the library, public headers, CMake package configuration, and CLI if it was built. Consumers can then use find_package(cvl) and link against cvl::cvl_lib.

docs.title: A minimal program
docs.text:
#include <cvl/cvl.h>

int main(void) {
    cvl_Mat img = cvl_imread("input.ppm");
    if (!img.data) {
        return 1;
    }

    cvl_Mat gray = cvl_cvt_color_new(&img, CVL_COLOR_RGB2GRAY);
    cvl_Mat binary = cvl_threshold_new(&gray, 128, 255, CVL_THRESH_BINARY);
    cvl_imwrite("binary.pgm", &binary);

    cvl_mat_free(&binary);
    cvl_mat_free(&gray);
    cvl_mat_free(&img);
    return 0;
}

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Include one header:

#include <cvl/cvl.h>

This includes CVL's core, image I/O, and image-processing interfaces. The headers provide extern "C" guards and can also be included from C++.

Page What it covers Core cvl_Mat, depths, allocation, and element access I/O cvl_imread, cvl_imwrite, and the formats they accept Image Processing Color conversion, thresholding, filtering, morphology, labeling, edge detection, etc.

Core types, constants, and matrix operations.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
typedef struct {
    int    height;
    int    width;
    int    channels;
    int    depth;
    size_t stride;
    void * data;
} cvl_Mat;

A unified matrix type for representing images, kernels, or other arbitrary matrix-like structures.

Rows are stored consecutively, with channels belonging to the same element stored next to one another. The address of row r is: (uint8_t *)mat->data + r * mat->stride.

The same type represents both images and other matrix data, such as floating-point kernels. For example, an 8-bit image and a 64-bit kernel are both cvl_Mat, distinguished by depth and channels.

Members

height Number of rows. width Number of columns. channels Number of channels per element. For example, an RGB image has three channels. depth Data type used to represent each channel. See cvl_depth_t. stride Number of bytes from one row to the next. data Pointer to the first byte of matrix storage. 
typedef enum cvl_format_t {
    CVL_FMT_UNKNOWN,
    CVL_FMT_PBM,
    CVL_FMT_PGM,
    CVL_FMT_PPM,
    CVL_FMT_PNG,
    CVL_FMT_JPG,
} cvl_format_t;

Enumeration of supported image formats.

Value Extension Description CVL_FMT_UNKNOWN - Unknown or unsupported image format. CVL_FMT_PBM .pbm Netpbm Portable Bitmap format for binary images. CVL_FMT_PGM .pgm Netpbm Portable Graymap format for grayscale images. CVL_FMT_PPM .ppm Netpbm Portable Pixmap format for colored images. CVL_FMT_PNG .png Portable Network Graphics, supported via stb. CVL_FMT_JPG .jpg Joint Photographic Experts Group, supported via stb. JPEG is a redundant verbocity that will not be condoned.

The PBM, PGM, and PPM formats are supported natively.

typedef enum cvl_depth_t {
    CVL_UINT8,
    CVL_32S,
    CVL_FLOAT32,
    CVL_FLOAT64,
} cvl_depth_t;

Enumeration of supported data types used to represent each matrix channel.

See cvl_cvt_depth() for converting between supported depths.

Value Description CVL_UINT8 8-bit unsigned integer (todo: rename: CVL_8U) CVL_32S 32-bit signed integer CVL_FLOAT32 32-bit floating point CVL_FLOAT64 64-bit floating point 
typedef enum cvl_color_conversion {
    CVL_COLOR_NONE,
    CVL_COLOR_RGB2GRAY,
    CVL_COLOR_BGR2GRAY,
    CVL_COLOR_GRAY2RGB,
    CVL_COLOR_GRAY2BGR,
} cvl_color_conversion;

Enumeration of supported color-space conversions.

See cvl_cvt_color() for converting between supported color spaces.

Value Source Channels Destination Channels Description CVL_COLOR_NONE — — No color conversion. CVL_COLOR_RGB2GRAY 3 1 Converts RGB color to grayscale. CVL_COLOR_BGR2GRAY 3 1 Converts BGR color to grayscale. CVL_COLOR_GRAY2RGB 1 3 Copies the grayscale value into each RGB channel. CVL_COLOR_GRAY2BGR 1 3 Copies the grayscale value into each BGR channel. 
typedef enum cvl_thresh_type {
    CVL_THRESH_BINARY,
    CVL_THRESH_BINARY_INV,
    CVL_THRESH_TRUNC,
    CVL_THRESH_TOZERO,
    CVL_THRESH_TOZERO_INV,
} cvl_thresh_type;

Enumeration of supported thresholding operations.

See cvl_threshold() for applying thresholds.

Mode Operation CVL_THRESH_BINARY src > thresh ? maxval : 0 CVL_THRESH_BINARY_INV src > thresh ? 0 : maxval CVL_THRESH_TRUNC src > thresh ? thresh : src CVL_THRESH_TOZERO src > thresh ? src : 0 CVL_THRESH_TOZERO_INV src > thresh ? 0 : src 
typedef enum cvl_interp_t {
    CVL_INTER_NEAREST,
    CVL_INTER_LINEAR,
} cvl_interp_t;

Enumeration of supported interpolation methods.

Value Description CVL_INTER_NEAREST Nearest-neighbor interpolation. CVL_INTER_LINEAR Bilinear interpolation.

docs.title: Image Processing
docs.text:
File reference for imgproc.h / imgproc.c.

Image processing operations.

Provides functions for common image processing tasks, including:

  • Color and type conversion: color-space conversion, depth conversion, thresholding.
  • Geomatric Transformations: rotation, cropping, resizing.
  • Morphological Transformations: dilation, erosion, opening, closing.
  • Connected Component Analysis: labeling and visualization.
  • Filtering and Convolution: correlation, convolution, box filtering, Gaussian blur, median blur.
  • Edge Detection: Sobel derivatives and gradient magnitudes.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
void cvl_cvt_color( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    int             code );

Converts a matrix to another color space.

Grayscale conversion uses the ITU-R BT.601 luminance coefficients.

Parameters

src Input matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have same size as src and the channel count required by code. code Color conversion code. See cvl_color_conversion. 
void cvl_cvt_depth( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    cvl_depth_t     ddepth,
                    double          alpha,
                    double          beta   );

Converts a matrix to another type with scaling.

Effectively: dst(x, y) = saturate_cast<ddepth>(alpha * src(x, y) + beta)

Parameters

src Input matrix. dst Output matrix. Must have the same dimensions and number of channels as src. ddepth Destination depth - type to convert to. See cvl_depth_t. alpha Multiplicative scale factor (1.0 for no change). beta Additive offset (0 for no change). 
void cvl_threshold( cvl_Mat *       img,
                    int             thresh,
                    int             maxval,
                    int             type   );

Applies a fixed-level threshold to each element.

Parameters

img Matrix to modify in place. thresh Threshold value. maxval Maximum output value used by binary thresholding. type Thresholding operation. See cvl_thresh_type. 
void cvl_rotate( const cvl_Mat * src,
                 cvl_Mat *       dst,
                 float           angle,
                 cvl_interp_t    interp );

Rotates a matrix clockwise around its center.

The dimensions of dst determine the output region. Source coordinates outside the input matrix are left unchanged in the destination matrix.

Orthogonal rotations use direct pixel rearrangement. Other angles use the specified interpolation method.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. angle Clockwise rotation angle, in degrees. interp Interpolation method. See cvl_interp_t. 
void cvl_invert( cvl_Mat *       img,
                 double          maxval );

Inverts matrix values relative to a specified maximum.

Each element's value becomes maxval - value. Values are processed independently for each channel.

Parameters

img Matrix to modify in place. maxval Maximum value used for inversion. 
void cvl_dilate( const cvl_Mat * src,
                 cvl_Mat *       dst,
                 int             ksize );

Applies morphological dilation to a matrix.

Replaces each element with the maximum value within its square neighborhood.

Border pixels are handled by replicating the nearest edge pixel.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square structuring element. 
void cvl_erode( const cvl_Mat * src,
                cvl_Mat *       dst,
                int             ksize );

Applies morphological erosion to a matrix.

Replaces each element with the minimum value within its square neighborhood.

Border pixels are handled by replicating the nearest edge pixel.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square structuring element. 
void cvl_open( const cvl_Mat * src,
               cvl_Mat *       dst,
               int             ksize );

Applies morphological opening to a matrix.

Performs erosion followed by dilation using the same square structuring element.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square structuring element. 
void cvl_close( const cvl_Mat * src,
                cvl_Mat *       dst,
                int             ksize );

Applies morphological closing to a matrix.

Performs dilation followed by erosion using the same square structuring element.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square structuring element. 
void cvl_crop( const cvl_Mat * src,
               cvl_Mat *       dst,
               int             r,
               int             c   );

Copies a rectangular region of interest into a destination matrix.

The region begins at (r, c) in the source matrix and has the dimensions of dst.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix defining the output dimensions. r Starting row in the source matrix. c Starting column in the source matrix. 
void cvl_resize( const cvl_Mat * src,
                 cvl_Mat *       dst,
                 cvl_interp_t    type );

Resizes a matrix using the specified interpolation method.

The destination matrix determines the output dimensions. Interpolation is performed independently for each channel.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix defining the output dimensions. type Interpolation method. See cvl_interp_t. 
int cvl_connected_components( const cvl_Mat * src,
                              cvl_Mat *       labels,
                              int             connectivity );

Labels connected foreground components in a binary image.

WHITE pixels are treated as background; all other pixels are treated as foreground.

Labels are assigned positive integer values, with zero reserved for background pixels.

Parameters

src Single-channel CVL_UINT8 binary source matrix. labels Single-channel CVL_32S destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. connectivity Pixel connectivity: 4 or 8.

Returns: Number of connected foreground components.

int cvl_color_components( cvl_Mat *       src,
                          const cvl_Mat * labels,
                          int             thresh );

Colors connected components that meet a minimum size.

Calculates the size of each labeled component and assigns a unique color to components containing at least thresh pixels. Components smaller than the threshold are unchanged.

Parameters

src Three-channel CVL_UINT8 image to modify. labels Single-channel CVL_32S component label matrix. thresh Minimum component size, in pixels.

Returns: Number of components meeting the minimum size.

void cvl_correlate( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    cvl_Mat *       kernel );

Applies a two-dimensional correlation operation.

The kernel is not flipped. Values outside the source matrix are treated as zero (constant-zero padding).

The output has the same dimensions, depth, and number of channels as the source matrix.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. kernel Single-channel CVL_FLOAT64 correlation kernel. 
void cvl_convolve( const cvl_Mat * src,
                   cvl_Mat *       dst,
                   cvl_Mat *       kernel );

Applies a two-dimensional convolution operation.

Convolves the source matrix with the specified kernel. Convolution flips the kernel by 180-degrees and then applies correlation.

Values outside the source matrix are treated as zero (constant-zero padding).

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. kernel Convolution kernel. 
void cvl_convolve_sep( const cvl_Mat * src,
                       cvl_Mat *       dst,
                       cvl_Mat *       kx,
                       cvl_Mat *       ky  );

Applies a separable two-dimensional convolution.

First convolves each row using the horizontal kernel, then convolves each column of the intermediate result using the vertical kernel.

This operation is useful when a two-dimensional filter can be represented as the product of two one-dimensional kernels.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. kx Horizontal one-dimensional kernel. ky Vertical one-dimensional kernel. 
void cvl_blur_box( const cvl_Mat * src,
                   cvl_Mat *       dst,
                   int             ksize,
                   bool            normalize );

Applies box filtering using a uniform square kernel.

Each output element is calculated from the sum of its neighborhood values. If normalize is true, the kernel weights are scaled by 1/(ksize * ksize), producing a mean filter.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square kernel. normalize Whether to normalize the kernel weights. 
void cvl_blur_mean( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    int             ksize );

Applies a normalized box filter (mean blur).

Each output element is the average of the values within its square neighborhood.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square kernel. 
void cvl_blur_gauss( const cvl_Mat * src,
                     cvl_Mat *       dst,
                     int             ksize,
                     double          sigma );

Applies Gaussian blur to a matrix.

If ksize is zero or negative, the kernel size is derived from sigma. If sigma is zero or negative, the standard deviation is derived from ksize.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix containing the blurred result. ksize Gaussian kernel width and height. Must be positive when sigma is not specified. sigma Standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution. Must be positive when ksize is not specified. 
void cvl_blur_median( const cvl_Mat * src,
                      cvl_Mat *       dst,
                      int             ksize );

Applies median filtering to a matrix.

Replaces each element with the median value of its square neighborhood. Border pixels are handled by replicating the nearest edge pixel.

Parameters

src Source matrix. dst Destination matrix. Must have the same dimensions as src. ksize Width and height of the square neighborhood, must be odd. 
void cvl_sobel( const cvl_Mat * src,
                cvl_Mat *       gx,
                cvl_Mat *       gy  );

Computes horizontal and vertical Sobel derivatives.

Applies the 3x3 Sobel operators to a single-channel source matrix to estimate intensity gradients in the horizontal and vertical directions.

Both output matrices contain signed gradient values represented using CVL_FLOAT64.

Parameters

src Single-channel source matrix. gx Destination matrix for horizontal gradients. Must be single-channel CVL_FLOAT64. gy Destination matrix for vertical gradients. Must be single-channel CVL_FLOAT64. 
void cvl_sobel_mag( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst );

Computes Sobel gradient magnitude.

Calculates horizontal and vertical Sobel derivatives and combines them using the Euclidean magnitude:

magnitude = sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy).

Parameters

src Single-channel source matrix. dst Single-channel destination matrix containing gradient magnitudes. 
cvl_Mat cvl_cvt_color_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                           int             code );

Converts a matrix to another color space and returns the result.

Grayscale conversion uses the ITU-R BT.601 luminance coefficients.

Parameters

src Input matrix. code Color conversion code. See cvl_color_conversion.

Returns: Newly allocated matrix containing the converted image.

cvl_Mat cvl_cvt_depth_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                           cvl_depth_t     ddepth,
                           double          alpha,
                           double          beta   );

Converts a matrix to another type with scaling and returns the result.

Effectively: dst(x, y) = saturate_cast<ddepth>(alpha * src(x, y) + beta)

Parameters

src Input matrix. ddepth Destination depth - type to convert to. See cvl_depth_t. alpha Multiplicative scale factor (1.0 for no change). beta Additive offset (0 for no change).

Returns: Newly allocated matrix containing the converted data.

cvl_Mat cvl_threshold_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                           int             thresh,
                           int             maxval,
                           int             type   );

Applies a fixed-level threshold to each element and returns the result.

Creates a copy of src and applies the specified thresholding operation.

Parameters

src Input matrix. thresh Threshold value. maxval Maximum output value used by binary thresholding. type Thresholding operation. See cvl_thresh_type.

Returns: Newly allocated thresholded matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_rotate_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                        float           angle,
                        cvl_interp_t    interp );

Rotates a matrix clockwise around its center and returns the result.

The output dimensions match the input dimensions, except for 90 and 270-degree rotations, which swap the dimensions. Non-orthogonal rotations may crop the corners of the image.

Parameters

src Source matrix. angle Clockwise rotation angle, in degrees. interp Interpolation method. See cvl_interp_t.

Returns: Newly allocated rotated matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_rotate_bound_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                              float           angle,
                              cvl_interp_t    interp );

Rotates a matrix clockwise while preserving the entire image.

Automatically expands the output dimensions to accommodate the rotated matrix without cropping its corners.

Parameters

src Source matrix. angle Clockwise rotation angle, in degrees. interp Interpolation method. See cvl_interp_t.

Returns: Newly allocated rotated matrix with expanded dimensions.

cvl_Mat cvl_crop_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                      int             r,
                      int             c,
                      int             h,
                      int             w   );

Extracts a rectangular region of interest into a new matrix.

Parameters

src Source matrix. r Starting row in the source matrix. c Starting column in the source matrix. h Height of the output region. w Width of the output region.

Returns: Newly allocated matrix containing the cropped region.

cvl_Mat cvl_resize_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                        int             height,
                        int             width,
                        cvl_interp_t    type   );

Resizes a matrix using the specified interpolation method and returns the result.

The destination matrix determines the output dimensions. Interpolation is performed independently for each channel.

Parameters

src Source matrix. height Height of the output matrix. width Width of the output matrix. type Interpolation method. See cvl_interp_t.

Returns: Newly allocated resized matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_correlate_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                           cvl_Mat *       kernel );

Applies two-dimensional correlation and returns the result.

Allocates a destination matrix with the same dimensions, depth, and number of channels as src.

Parameters

src Source matrix. kernel Correlation kernel.

Returns: Newly allocated matrix containing the correlation result.

cvl_Mat cvl_convolve_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                          cvl_Mat *       kernel );

Applies two-dimensional convolution and returns the result.

Allocates a destination matrix with the same dimensions, depth, and number of channels as src.

Parameters

src Source matrix. kernel Convolution kernel.

Returns: Newly allocated matrix containing the convolution result.

cvl_Mat cvl_blur_box_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                          int             ksize,
                          bool            normalize );

Applies box filtering and returns the result.

Parameters

src Source matrix. ksize Width and height of the square kernel. normalize Whether to normalize the kernel weights.

Returns: Newly allocated blurred matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_blur_mean_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                           int             ksize );

Applies mean blur and returns the result.

Each output element is the average of the values within its square neighborhood.

Parameters

src Source matrix. ksize Width and height of the square kernel.

Returns: Newly allocated blurred matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_blur_gauss_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                            int             ksize,
                            double          sigma );

Applies Gaussian blur and returns the result.

Parameters

src Source matrix. ksize Gaussian kernel width and height, or zero to derive the size from sigma. sigma Standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution, or zero to derive it from ksize.

Returns: Newly allocated blurred matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_blur_median_new( const cvl_Mat * src,
                             int             ksize );

Applies median filtering and returns the result.

Parameters

src Source matrix. ksize Width and height of the square neighborhood, must be odd.

Returns: Newly allocated median-filtered matrix.

cvl_Mat cvl_sobel_mag_new( const cvl_Mat * src );

Computes Sobel gradient magnitude and returns the result.

Parameters

src Single-channel source matrix.

Returns: Newly allocated single-channel matrix containing gradient magnitudes.

void cvl_cvt_color( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    int             code );

void cvl_cvt_depth( const cvl_Mat * src,
                    cvl_Mat *       dst,
                    cvl_depth_t     ddepth,
                    double          alpha,
                    double          beta   );

Converts a matrix to another type with scaling.

Effectively: dst(x, y) = saturate_cast(α * src(x, y) + β)

Parameters

src Input matrix. dst Output matrix. ddepth Type to convert to. alpha Scale factor (1.0 for no change). beta Value added to scaled values (0 for no change). 
void cvl_threshold( cvl_Mat *       img,
                    int             thresh,
                    int             maxval,
                    int             type   );

Applies a fixed-level threshold to each element — determined by type.

Parameters

img Matrix to apply a threshold to. thresh Threshold value. maxval Maximum value. type Type of thresholding operation to perform. See cvl_thresh_type. 
void cvl_rotate( const cvl_Mat * src,
                 cvl_Mat *       dst,
                 float           angle,
                 cvl_interp_t    interp );

File reference for io.h / io.c.

Reading and writing images.

Based on template from (V2.2 by Marc Pomplun on 10/19/2013).

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
cvl_Mat cvl_imread( const char * filename );

Reads an image from the specified file.

The image format is detected from the file header, not the file extension.

Parameters

filename Path to read the image from.

Returns: A CVL_UINT8 matrix containing the decoded image, or an empty matrix on failure.

int cvl_imwrite( const char * filename,
                 cvl_Mat *    img      );

Writes an image to the specified file.

The image format is determined from the file extension.

Format Read Write Requirements PBM binary P4 .pbm 1 channel, CVL_UINT8, pixels must be 0 or 255 PGM binary P5 .pgm 1 channel, CVL_UINT8 PPM binary P6 .ppm 3 channels, CVL_UINT8 PNG stb .png CVL_UINT8, 1 to 4 channels JPEG stb .jpg CVL_UINT8, 1 or 3 channels, no padding between pixels

JPEG is written at quality 90.

Parameters

filename Path to write the image to. img Image to write.

Returns: 0 on success, 1 on failure.
